title: Beginning in Bend
body:
Been a month since leaving White Salmon, WA to set out on this adventure. Still calling Washington home for now, but really the road is going to be home this spring and summer (though Alaska is always my real home, and our eventual destination this summer). 

The Alaskan winters finally got me to leave in 2022 to try something a little warmer in the region, close to fam and friends. After a stint in Portland, two stints in White Salmon (an unforgettable adventure or two on of their own), it's time to embark on an epic roadtrip with Wojo (the star and voice of this journal hereafter).

We'll be exploring the southwest, playing it by ear, and trying to save money to eventually land somewhere more permanent. We'll log our travels and experiences here as often as we can, but not too much. Next stop will be back up in The Gorge to take care of some business and see fam before really heading out.

The site and our voices will evolve over time. Please reach out directly if you know me or via the anonymous form in the Wandering Wojo panel on the main page here. 

Wish us luck! Hit us up! Send suggestions, essential albums, or whatever else you think might enhance the experience. We're excited, a little nervous, but really ready to have the roadtrip of a lifetime!

title: Touching Base
body:
Started feeling a bit antsy in Central Oregon… Ready to get on the road but taking care of odds and ends, errands, paperwork, setting up the truck, all while he’s working full time and we’re hopping from place to place, crashing guest rooms.. odd how this can feel claustrophobic. 

Felt amazing to get on the road, even if just on a trip back north to The Gorge. Just a tiny taste of what’s to come. Half-way through the ride I got a little restless, stuck in this mesh backpack the big guy got me. He let me out and holy shit… sounds, trees and lights moving faster than I ever realized they could. He let me sit on his lap towards the end of the ride while he sang with the big sounds, “You’ve got a friend… ‘aint it good to know…”

Now it’s just biding time in the hot room upstairs while it rains outside. I trust he’ll get our space all fixed up for the next leg of the ride. Meanwhile, I think I can see that he’s got some big feelings, maybe some sadness being back where he had his biggest dreams and almost made it all come together, but not quite.

I can see his eyes get watery sometimes, but I know he’s been through tough times and can handle this. He says his shoulder tat is about flexibility, agility, resilience… “Whatever way you throw him, he lands upright”. Anyway… kinda like me, I guess. Being a cat and all.

Still, I can hear him laughing and chatting with the fam he has here and knows it puts him at ease, maybe reminding him that it’s not just me who cares and looks after him. Seems like he loves them as much as I love him. Ugh, what a swirl of feelings. Let’s hope he finds some ease and smiles… maybe recharges a bit so we can start this adventure on the right paw.

title: The Precipice
body:
The adventure really begins tomorrow morning. It's been nice staying with family in The Gorge, buttoning up odds and ends, getting some laughs and hugs in. Even got to visit Black Cat one more time before she embarks on her final journey. What an opportunity to practice optimism and letting go (of everything, wonderful and sad alike). 

Sounds like we'll be staying in a campground with power, showers and even a restaurant, in Northern California for the first week. A nice opportunity to get a feel for our setup and what might be missing. 

It's been nice staying in the biggest house I've ever seen, with my own extra-warm room upstairs. I'm a bit anxious about being outdoors, but I dunno... I've acclimated to new spaces before and this might turn out to be not so bad. At least there will be a ton of new smells. 

Anyway, just touching base and getting this pin on the map before we move along. I sure love the people here, friends and family alike. Maybe I'll get to see them again soon.

title: Day 1... Woah, Jo...
body:
Welll... we landed. First real roadtripping day in the books. I hated the car ride. Flat out. I barked, yelped, moaned, until I found a nook in the back seat I could smash my face into and just close my eyes until it was over. I peed in my carrier... just seconds after I was in my litterbox. I don't know... I was frazzled... it was loud. I felt bad, but I cried wolf too many times and the big guy couldn't tell I really meant it when I finally had to go. 

We're in the tent now, listening to a stream and the occasional train pass by. The big guy grabbed dinner in this cute train car restaurant at the place we're staying and said he loved it... hippies playing sax jazz and guitar bossa nova... Ultra burger and a beer to wrap up the long day of driving. I guess he deserved it after putting up with the piss fest... even if he did make me wait in the car this morning while he visited and said he "felt great... god damn... what a trip... love love, happy hug blah blah." Humans... 

Anyway, he'll be back to work tomorrow morning, and we'll find our rhythm on the road. I'm beat... need some sleep. More journaling to come as we hang here a week.... I'm so tired I'm rhyming... a rhyming cat... anyway, gnight world.

Morning Update: I slept like a rock up in that tent... I think we both did. Still having a rough time with the sounds this moving house makes sometimes... but I ate some food and I'm starting to get curious about the world. I dunno, maybe this won't be half bad...

title: OOoookay
body:
Oooookay... today wasn't so bad. The big guy took pics of me to share, but there were plenty that weren't captured. I got to stretch my legs, sunbathe, scratch trees, eat grass, watch birds... And then a nice long nap in the truck. 

The decompression seems to finally be starting to hit... what now? There's no one. Actually, that's not true, Big guy's bestie happened to stop by for a quick visit. That was truly special and unexpected (see the cheesy pic of them hamming it up, eh they're alright).  

He also has some bright squares that his people seem to talk through with him. They show up from time to time to cheer him on, and me too it seems. The fun one with the food hair even spent some square time with him today... I can tell how much that puts him at ease and tugs on strings. Sounds like others even send messages through our journal, without even including their names... Anonymous encouragement feels so real. Thanks everyone 🫂

But... how the hell did I end up homeless with a 40 year old human in tow...? He says he's house hunting... But how to hunt when you don't even know where, or what for? Land to build? House to buy? Why? Why not? Maybe he needs to think more like a cat... we know how to hunt... 

Anyway, too many questions... the decompression seems to have paused. Think it's time to clean and get cozy for the evening. Maybe close my eyes and just feel grateful until I crap out. So damn deeply grateful.... 💤

title: Morning Time Now
body:
It's morning time now. lLstening to all of the sounds out here... chainsaws, a nearby river, birds, people... It's nice but still a lot to take in. So, yeah, I'm sitting on the big guy's lap, resting my chin on his arm, patiently waiting for the sun to come around and warm us up. Crazy how it can be so cold at night here, and so hot during the day!

Love seeing all the nice anonymous messages come in from our journal page! What a treat to be so loved...

title: Finding Ease
body:
Spent most of the day outside on the longer leash the big guy got me. Actually went for a little stroll with him and I gotta admit... once I got past the fear of the big sounds... I kind liked it. Lots of grass to chew, smells to sniff, bugs to chase. Not too shabby... No shab at all really.

Honestly, not much to report today besides finding a bit of space, relaxation, ease. Sometimes it's not about a flashy day, or grandiose things. Seems like sometimes the most grandiose is when we get to breathe, or at least remember that it's possible to breathe. 

How cool to be this fortunate... to just have trees show up... sunlight... hugs, kind and considerate messages of support and admiration, collaboration with good people. Screw the news... I choose this.

title: Planning...
body:
What a lazy day... but that's what cats crave. Still... Been thinking about the next destination. 

While doing a little research, its starting to feel a bit like Truman when he planned to go to Fiji... gas prices are suddenly exploding, a multi-week heat wave exactly where we're going... potential crash pads suddenly not responding... kinda like "fire at the plant!", a broken down bus... a freak localized storm directly over head...

Hmmmm... OK so it'll be unbearably hot and expensive in the Southwest... So we'll follow the temps and roam around here. Find some hot springs, visit the coast, pop into the mountains... hell we could go to Nebraska. Right?

Anyway, feels nice to let go and let it all happen. No need to get angry when the red dot you caught isn't really under your paw, but is actually back on the wall... Let's just enjoy the chase.

title: Family in Nevada
body:
Well... what an amazing Saturday we had... On a whim we blasted out of Shasta and down into the super warm valley below. Stunning green rolling hills, lush with plants and smells for feline nasal delight!! 

After rolling through that humid warmth we began back up the mountains through trees and into desert and snow to see some of the big guy's family tribe. 

They didn't see it, but I saw him get glassy eyes as he felt grateful for the incredible hospitality as they fed him and shared stories. We even got to sleep in a bed and meet two weird looking cats that were so excited and super sweet. 

Anyway, just a quick stop on our way south. More to come this evening. What an amazing whirlwind... amazing food for the soul. Can't wait to come back and hang a bit more :) 

"Shower the people you love with love."

title: Straddled
body:
We drove out of Reno and up through the Sierra Mountains, behind Yosemite, to keep a bit more cool today. A stunning drive that I savagely meowed through in its entirety. 

Now we're on the edge of the heatwave just south of us, straddled by the Sequoia National Forest to the west and Death Valley to the east. Its stunningly beautiful here, and honestly, the whole campsite has ground that's like natural kitty litter... maybe I'll experiment with that a bit in the next few days.

The plan is to hang tight and let the big guy work before mobbing out through the Mojave Desert to Flagstaff where it's higher and cooler, and then Grand Canyon Thursday evening. We'll do some off-grid camping and canyon exploring for a while after that.

Or at least that's what we're thinking. That can always change :)

On another note... What is meaning? Why the compulsion for closeness, comfort, familiarity? It's fascinating to observe oneself once all routine and regularity is removed. Knee-jerk reactions, creature comforts, annoyances, pleasant surprises. They just show up... And then decisions are made and then more things show up. What a stream. But what do I know? Why so contemplative? I'm just a friggin cat... I do notice that I'm getting more comfortable in the truck though, sitting on the console touching my nose to the big guy's arm. And with those weird big loud short faced "cats" at some people's houses... I guess they're not so bad. And all these new places and smells... I even got to stick my teeny nose tip out the window today to smell the passing mountain air.... Not too shabby... no shab at all. 

The balance of the familiar with the fresh is a fascinating back and forth... a dancing knife's edge I guess.. or cat's claw? Tooth? Poop?

title: Haht T'day
body:
We gaht haht t'day. Had to make plenty of use of that cold air inside the truck... And plenty of lazy laying around in the shade, with the breeze. Holy cow. 

But, the big guy had to do his screen work and it was otherwise low key. He painted our journal's web address on the tent for others to see. Not sure why tbh... But, why not? Who knows what random connections come of it 🤷‍♂️

Been thinking about that feeling of being rushed a lot. Seems like a lot of it has to do with whatever is going on outside (heat, cold, loud, the pressures of AI making everyone obsolete and the impetus it puts on people to do MORE, FASTER, NOW or face financial ruin)... But also how the inside is ordered (or not).

Anyway that rushed feeling sucks. Enjoying a fresh breeze, a bird, clean cool water, someone showing you how much you mean to them, the smell of spring wildflowers, shelter when it's needed, and freedom otherwise.

But so many of those pleasantries are bought with funds. Funds that may go away.... Seems like a tribe of great people are the way through that... trading, supporting, loving. And here we are, the big guy and I, far from that loving tribe, cooking in the desert. Maybe we have to fling ourselves far out away from our loves in order to someday offer them more, if we're lucky enough to find them again. Or maybe to break patterns, learn more... I dunno.

Or maybe we're just here, doing this, and that's ok. Come what may.

title: Death Valley Tomorrow
body:
Today was a chill as they come. Warm but not too hot. The big guy really tested out the solar/starlink setup and its not too shabby (i.e. no shab). He also jury-rigged some cardboard flaps under the tent to keep it from buzzing and flopping on the drive. Crossing our fingers on that one...

SO, the plan was to mob out 8 hours tomorrow after work, straight to Flagstaff. Screw that. I think the big guy took pity on me (and his stinky ass feet) and booked us a one night stay in Vegas. That cuts each leg into 4 hours. Then, we'll be overland off-grid camping for three nights near the entrance to the Grand Canyon! Maybe finally this big oaf will get me out on some hikes in my cat backpack!

So that's settled. He also had a great call with his boss today, talking through some deep/pressing things at work. The big guy really seems to feel rushed, pressured, worried, stressed, about staying relevant and useful. I can see it robbing him of his ability to enjoy things. This trip is so special and unique... he better figure it out before it's all behind him and he's rushed through it. 

Anyway I'm here cleaning myself in the cool tent while the big guy takes this down for me. I hope you all are digging the new "Your 2 cents" menu in the journal here... The polls, Same ability to message us and now the ability to help support us with gas/treat money. You can even direct how the big guy spends those funds in your donation message! GET ME SOME FISH! He'll take pics and make sure to post them in the next day's story for you :) 

Anyway, hug someone if you can. Talk to cool strangers if they're around (big guy met someone from his home town today!). Revisit past connections that you may have been hasty about (they may surprise you)...

People and our connections with them are all that matter it seems. And loving, charitable, curious fun connections (not the shit stabbing ass ripping kind). 

I love you guys and I think the big dude does also. Hit us up in the new menu!

title: Las Vegas
body:
The big guy thought he'd be clever and drive in the evenings after work. He thought he'd even push through Death Valley, thinking it wouldn't be too bad. 

I melted like furry butter... 108 degrees and no AC for much of it to keep the engine cooled off. That kinda heat is no joke it seems... 

Anyway, it was nice but also a little sad to say goodbye to the site we were at in Lone Pine, but I can't say I'll miss the dust... sheesh. 

Not a long journal entry tonight. We're just stopping over on our way to the Grand Canyon. Seems like there are some really nice people, and really cool hikes near here though. Might be worth swinging back through... 

The big guy was goofy excited and wanted to get a bunch of pics with me in Death Valley... He's gonna post them here but, just know (if you can't tell form the photos) that I wasn't feeling it. 

I'll touch base with yawls tomorrow. 

Oh PS... The big guy just mentioned that we're in the birthplace of my namesake, Wowajahowitz, the cat he grew up with, born the same year as him. I guess he named me after him because I look just like the elder Woj. Pretty cool. Whatever.

title: Diné Today
body:
5 years ago today, the big guy's step dad passed. He was an amazing guy, with a wild story, and a huge heart. Five years ago the big guy couldn't be there in person as Nakaii passed, but he dug a grave for him for when his ashes came back home to Resurrection Bay. 

Today the big guy's fam is back home in Alaska and we're out here in the middle of nowhere just south of the Grand Canyon's South entrance. 

From what Grandma says Nakaii was the coyote, but also came to people in dreams as a white horse or riding a white horse...

 Tonight, after the big dude gets all set up in his tent, I hear footsteps nearby and then he shouts out "hello?? Someone out there?"

He unzips his tent flaps and shines a light but it just lights up the screen... can't see anything. So as the footsteps continue he unzips the main tent door flap and sees a moonlit white horse walking off into the dark. 

There was one time Nakaii did the big dude an incredibly huge favor and said "You're Diné today." he'll forever be grateful. 

Tonight we sleep with the coyotes and horses, and the sound of people yelling at them in the distance. We remember and love Nakaii.

title: Constant Change
body:
What a day. I was on a meowing TIRADE the first half of the day. Those coyotes chilled me to the bone, and the big guy was up in the tent having his own spiritual night... damn... I just woke up anxious, thirsty and ready to make it known. 

Big dude did his best and I eventually calmed down, just in time for him to rip me from my newfound cozy blanket bowl and out into the most MASSIVE litterbox I think must ever exist... "Glam Canyon"? I dunno... I don't give a shit. He was excited but I just wanted to sleep... so he put me back, thank gah.

He did bring me back a piece of his bison prime rib though... and I dunno, maybe he's back in my good graces because of it. Eh, I know he loves me...

He said there was a plaque mentioning that this canyon is a sea of change... constant erosion and reformation. Kinda like our world of late, or I guess always? I mean... if I'm being honest, I guess each moment does see new things arise and everything else pass. I'm not sure there really even is an actual moment... just a flow... then what's noticing it? When I look for "me" I just notice that looking is happening... and everything is rushing by... even memories seem to only happen now, like sounds do, in the present, like the past isn't anywhere else but right here. 

Ok fuck sorry I'm just cat mambling... Steak, meow, sleep, bye.

title: What a Rush!
body:
"What a practice" he says... so dramatic... But I do see him wound up. He was so ready to have a weekend break and what does he do? He crams as much of the Grand Canyon experience into 1.5 days, and drives/works frantically on personal projects for the other .5 days of the weekend (his own personal music streaming website 🤦‍♂️ kladg.com, and updating this journal to look better on a computer)...

I'm here trying to lead by example... BE LAZY! Layabout! Stop rushing... but he doesn't seem to get it. He came home completely wiped out after his canyon hike... I just sat there and looked at him... "really?

title: Red Red & Red All Over
body:
Well, I'm REALLY relaxing. Really. Big guy got us a little motel room on old Route 66 near Downtown Flagstaff for a few nights, took off my harness and SHEEEheeeesh does that feel good. Not too shabby at all. NO shab...

Just a quick drive today from the canyon down to Sedona for a little lunch, he got a massage, and a tiny "hike" up a hill for a view. 

It's so RED around there. Beautiful. "The Red Road" Nakaii would always talk about walking along, a good path. Anyway, a few days to recharge, let the big dude focus on work, visit some friends nearby, watch Gunsmoke and just lay around, stretch my legs, maybe even get the zoomies if I feel like it. I don't even give a care.

I've mentioned it a few times (it may be an ongoing theme in this journal, not sure), but I think the big dude is starting to really try to relax. He's not there yet, but he is really trying. A massage was a nice start, but he needs to find time to read like he did just a month ago. I guess reading time turned into driving time, and that's ok. But also meditation, maybe even naps would be helpful? It's only 6:30 on Sunday and he's committed to just hanging in the room with me rather than cramming more activities into his day. Baby steps.

title: The Hunt
body:
Been zooming all over this morning, and last night. New things to hunt in a new space, and all...

But now we're sitting on the bed for sunrise, listening. Fridge buzz, cars passing, people mumbling, water trickling. It's all right here... the trick is that it seems like it's over "there". Everything is right here, and nothing is missing. How could it be? In the deepest sense, this really is everything. It's as good, and bad as it could possibly be, right now, because nothing is missing. There's nothing to hunt for or find that isn't already right here.

That in mind... I'll clean myself now. At least until that pesky light shows up again and needs to be caught!

Oh... and check out the new poll if you haven't already (close this story and click the "Your 2 Cents" button up top).

title: Ease Please!
body:
This is what I imagine goes on in his head - "Beebaboo.. Good boieee, yeah, okaaaay buddie, springtime in The Shire bub... Southwest, friends, Mordor... not too shabby... no shab, Yeahhhhh buddy" and on and on... 

I also heard him mambling about "what are we doing buddy?" and then realizing something about "this is it". It just goes... and wanting to make my cat life as awesome as he can, because apparently he thinks doing things like that really matter.

I love that he relentlessly cares, not just about me but everyone... but it's a heavy load giving so many shits. "Lighten up and let go" a wise someone once told him. Easier said than done. I do wish he'd just enjoy  rather than trying to ensure enjoying. 

Big hearts + crispy minds are a hell of a combo. It'll be nice to get some time with dear friends and fam in the next couple weeks, and even some regular sitting meditation, all ways to be right here more than up there in that swirl. 

More events and pics to come. We're still laying low and taking care for another night (unless the person violently vomiting all night next door doesn't stop...) Oh and a shoutout to Granny for the treats she tucked into the Big Guy's truck. Thank you!!!

And another shout out to the big dude's sister. she has a weird looking cat and sent a pic of them two up in Alaska, where we're headed in a couple months it seems! We're so damn lucky to have so many amazing people. Sheesh... If you wanna share your own pics/stories, use the messaging feature in the Your 2 Cents menu at the top of the page when you close this story!! Just remember to include your name/contact info if you don't wanna be anonymous!

title: Where the Wind Blows...
body:
Final night in Flagstaff. Feels like the cool wind is blowing us south to warmer temps, just in time for visits in Tucson, just as it has been this whole trip. I think we're both ready to get moving again. 

There was a moment earlier, when it just felt kinda neutral, blank... No rush, nor any feeling of being held up... just... here. That's kinda nice. Seems to leave space for savoring, and maybe making measured choices, or just... sitting. 

I think we'll just do that. I'll sit in this window sill watching trains and cars pass by, and the big dude will sit and notice, sipping on and savoring everything showing up right now.

title: Tucson
body:
I think I have to say... I love the truck. Never would have guessed it after the first day... remembering shoving my face into the crack between the seat and the door... But not today... Today I roamed, let the Arizona air rush into my tiny nose as it flew by the window. I even laid on the big guy's lap for a while, and then when it got dark, I stood on my hind legs, front paws on the dash looking out into the darkness, eager to see what would come our way. 

I guess there's something to be said for embarking (emeowing?) in the face of the unknown, the sad, scary, uncertain, loud wilderness. At some point, it seems like, once you're out of the comfort patterns and routines long enough, you realize that we're always embarking. We just lull ourselves into feeling safe among the recognizable. 

But... isn't everything always fresh? Aren't we fooling ourselves or glossing over nuance in order to apply the stamp of familiarity? Are we really living when we're comfortable or is that just a little temple-of-taking-things-for-grated that we've built? Maybe that's what they mean about true comfort being within, rather than what we build around us... maybe that's letting go and acceptance? 

Wow. Er... I mean, meow.

title: Fire in The Desert Sky
body:
Got to roll in some bird shit today. Chilled in a cubby. Saw some lizards. This place is pretty damn chill I'd say. Big guy did his work, saw the inexorable march of automation creeping, seeping into every nook. Did  laundry (thank god...), bought some fruit and smoked oysters, and then caught up with a dear friend on a whim and felt really good about people. Funny how life tends to put amazing people in front of you when you least expect it.

And maybe its not that they're making a killing or are firing on all cylinders in the conventional sense, but more like they happen to have amazing insight and are on a part of the journey that rhymes with your own, enough that both parties can learn/enjoy a thing or two from each other, even just a nice walk and a real chat. As Mr. Garcia (and Mr. Knowles) once stated so beautifully, "Once in a while you get shown the light in the strangest of places if you look at it right."

Speaking of shining the light, we saw these huge skittering brown bugs showing up when it got dark... I started hunting them as the big guy kinda flipped out at the sight of them. I dunno, they just kinda walk around, eat and drink but the big guy seemed grossssssed out. I think even he was surprised by how much they made his hair stand on end.

Anyway, time to try to get some sleep...

title: Friends are Good :)
body:
Well, friends are good. If not for the generosity of their time and space, their recommendations for cool spots and great music, then for the ease they seem to invite us into and the laughs and hugs we get to share with them. I know the big guy does that for me, and I can see his friends and fam do that for him. It's cool to watch him remember this.

Aside from that, today was crazy lazy while the big dude worked, until later that evening when we went into the back yard and hunted for all kinda of little shitheads and crazies. He'll post a few pics of me in my element. 

Now that the weekend has kicked off, there will be hikes and truck cleaning, furniture moving and maybe even a house show with a bunch of folks from the big dude's hometown of Anchorage. We'll see what falls into place!

Until then, please enjoy most of all, the pic of Granny with her new "Woj" kitchen towel. She's the one who sneaks me treats!! Love that lady! GAH we're lucky...

title: XyloJamz
body:
Well, they came back with stories. I did more lazing here (tending to the cut on my little paw from hunting around the yard the other night). But, the big dude and his friend went hiking among the saguaros, near where a Beatle used to live... (some McCartney guy...) Found a rainbow lizard, some cool rocks, his friend got stung in the face by a bee, found some tacos and some live xylophone jams, met a water pro and a cheese slanger at a biker bar, ate some of the best tacos ever, learned about a nonsense wedding speech given that was inspired by the big guy's own gibberish... Sounds like it was a mellow, heartfelt, heartifilling, eclectic experience. They topped it off with some exquisite cheeses and wild foraged cacao chocolate. Can't make this shit up I guess. 

Anyway, one more day of chillin while the big dude reorders his truck, our home, and gets back on the road. It's been nice to stretch out and take it easy, but it seems life is pulling us onward. "Into the great wide open... under the skies of blue"

title: Harness, Be Gone
body:
The big dude took off my harness yesterday. MAN that felt good. He really massaged and pet where the harness was and it was such a nice relief. Seems like that's what his friends do for him, in a less literal but maybe more personal way. 

There was Sunday of book club, truck/trip organization, scratch local lunch (I had a new chicken kibble), Calls with family, more visits form amazingly considerate local friends... I finally met a dear friend of the bug dude's - Myken - an effortlessly genuine and deeply caring person... like the core tribe the big dude grew up with. Feels almost surreal and reassuring to realize there are people out there like that, and who we get to call friends.

He then met more of Michela's amazing crew at a mind blowing, tear-jerking, beautiful local play, meandering through a park with scene after scene encouraging a newly trained vet to stick around on this fantastical island of magical animals which he was feeling inadequate and too anxious to treat. Come to find out he was only selling himself short and was in fact far more capable than he let himself admit, and decided to stick around after all...

That summary does no justice to the ample care and sincerity each of the kids and adults gave to this. Seems like the play really moved the big dude, and made him more deeply consider himself on this roadtrip journey we're on. When will he ever realize that he's pretty decent and more than enough, he's plenty. 

Anyway, he's also got bug bites all over his feet. He doesn't quite know how to express how much his friends here mean to him, but really wants to. Tucson is leaving a big mark...

title: Beautiful Mud
body:
Well, it was a long evening of driving and reflecting. We headed out from Tucson with a reordered truck that feels much more spacious. Maybe the big dude reordered himself a little too. 

We saw rain for the first time on our trip... over a month since a sprinkle, and we find it in the New Mexico desert in the pitch black. We pulled over and camped on some BLM land just north of Truth or Consequences and drove a bit more in the morning to the southern outskirts of Albuquerque. 

The smell this morning, of the satiated desert earth and plants was just beautiful. A stunning "smellrise" as the sun also rose and lit the rolling mountains and clouds. Not a bad way to start the day. 

I'm gonna hang in the truck here and get reacquainted while he works the first half of the day in a cafe. I'll be thinking about that "dog?" I heard and smelled back in Tucson, and that amazingly gracious and generous friend who hosted us - Michela. What a special world going on over there, with lizards in the back, cacti, doves galore, story time, piles of laughs and just good vibes all around. 

I think much of the drive had (for him) to do with accepting the passing of everything that arises, including amazing visits and smiles. Funny... just as we're headed to visit a Zen Center in Santa Fe :) 

P.S... Looks like it's been one month since our first entry in Bend Oregon. Only (already) a month in and months to go. What a privilege!

title: Sacrament
body:
We woke just north of Truth or Consequences this morning after a night of heavy rain. I already mentioned how beautifully it smelled. 

We drove before the big guy had to work and a little more after he finished. Finally landed in old Santa Fe (Holy Faith). At his Granny’s suggestion, the first place he visited was the Loretto Chapel with its self-supporting spiral staircase. 

He wasn’t sure what to expect, and with only 15 min before closing, he wasn’t sure if the $5 entry fee would be worth it. 

Turns out it was. 

It was a beautiful chapel, obviously so sincerely cared for and constructed, with beautiful stained glass, arches, sanctuary, stations of the cross, with so much attention to detail. He hadn’t been in a church like this since he was a kid. It felt to him less like money built it and more like love and true reverence.

Born and raised Catholic, the big dude and his fam opted for individual spiritual exploration (starting at age 9 for him). His reading of Nietzsche eventually led him to earn a degree in philosophy where he found reductionism, logic, and an ethical atheism rooted in awe of the natural world, recursiveness, Hofstadter’s Strange Loops and Gödelian incompleteness only to realize via Zen meditation (and the “koan” of Chalmers’s Hard Problem) that the only claims that can be made have to do with what’s presenting right now (Zen and Socrates rhyming). 

In the Chapel today though it all struck him in a deep way… like a chorus after a climbing series of key changes… Childhood faith and wonder -> An early adulthood of rigorous and genuinely curious investigation -> Mid-life reflection and deep appreciation -> Newfound humbling awe and wonder. 

A climbing staircase returning to its previous position but with a broader vantage, built on itself… An expanding experience, relying on its own cohesion and structure to revisit the same lateral space in cycles, and with wisdom as it rises, relying only on the integrity of its continual, reflexive inward turn. Totality curling back to understand and love. 

Nietzsche’s aphorism of the progression from being an infant (open-minded and helplessly at the whim of everything), to the camel, eager to embark and carry the load… to take life head on, and eventually on to the masterful, graceful, equanimous lion (my favorite, being a feline, myself), only for the lion to experience a humble and holistic realization that the master truly is still (and always was) a child in light of everything, experiencing beginner’s mind, realizing (as infants effortlessly do) selflessness… no self, expansive unity… reflexive egoism… selfishness for an infinitely expansive and perfectly inclusive “self”. Humble compassion. 

This felt like a return not to dogma and arbitrary structures of control (as he came to see religion as a teen), but to reverence of and deference to the inevitably present quality of experience as it continuously, generously unfolds.

He took no shortcut. He wholeheartedly experienced every station of this journey, from hardline atheism, to being the whitespace of a tree’s branches and curling back to drink oneself from the inviting arms of the lupine. From inexpressible love, to almost sitting out at night to freeze to death. What kept the wheel turning was the humble curiosity about what love might lie around the next corner, and what love he might be able to give, in the next moment. The circuit is made, always deciding to (as Zarathustra would say) “go under” once more. 

This week “going under” looks like sits and dharma talks at the local Zen Center. Five years ago he connected with them online in his darkest times, accepting wholeheartedly that he might not ever connect with others in person again. How far we've come :) We’ll see what he finds and what he lets go of.

Or, more concisely, check out Dan Reeder’s song, “Born a Worm” (included at the end of the images section).

The big dude is dictating to me (obviously) and I’m doing my best with these damn paws to get it all down. I kinda like how I’m all three though (infant, “camel”, lion) as a young eager cat buddy with a bounty of confidence that comes from within. 

So… he had a big day… Jesus… 

I, on the other hand, had as calm a day as ever. I don’t really know what he’s on about. 

Cat. 
Meow. 
Zen?

title: No Shab
body:
It was a day of working in the sun (lazing sooo contentedly in the truck), followed by a trip to the Zen Center so the big guy could experience it in person. 

A beautiful place, hosting extremely lovely and heartfelt people. 

Not sure there could be anything more Zen than the big guy feeling like nature and being on the road feels more "in tune" than being in the zendo. 

Deep gratitude and respect, and much more sitting meditation and more regular practice will resume now. But, out in the world, among the muck and the sun, vast canyons and ants hauling away some jerky he dropped, just feels more like "it". 

Anyway that was him. the highlight of MY day was seeing this MASSIVE rabbit (hare?) just outside the truck! The damn thing was bigger than me and its ears as big as my arms! It barely hopped and more like walked with enormously long legs. Too bad this glass was keeping me in, otherwise I woulda... I coulda... I'da ripped that thing apart and brought it back to share with the big guy... "HOLD ME BACK"! 

The big dude mentioned to his mom on the phone that he's been making the trip all about him... like this hasn't really been my journal. Kinda cool he recognized that. His cousin sent us our FIRST donation. $25 smackaroonies... Big guy says he's gonna start making the trip stops more about me, and cat-friendly experiences. Oh and he's gonna spend that cold hard cash on either some dope ass treats or entry to a cat-catered experience. We'll see... 

If y'all donate, include a note if you want him to spend it in any certain way. Fix me UP!

Anyway, yeah... not too shabby a day at all. No shab, baby.

title: Jailbreak
body:
I busted out. He didn't even realize until I was across the campsite. No leash, no hot truck air, just freedom. Grit on my paws, smells rushing by, hot sun beating down, ants and birds and turds and just... open. 

I kept just ahead of his reach until I got under a camp table and he seemed to genuinely just be joining me. He voice sounded friendly. But... holy shit did he pick me up and rush me back to the truck. Bopped the fuck out of my nose and told me "You just can't do that dude... its not safe... you don't understand what's out there"... Asshole. I'M A CAT. I'm curious, I hunt. I don't give a shit what's out there unless I can kill it. 

Anyway, back in the truck I just look out the back window as he drives off somewhere. Ends up using the funds cousin D sent to buy me a flea and tick collar. On the ride he said he was sorry... that I was right, but "we need to do it the right way, the safe way, with a leash and bug prevention." Ok fine. 

So, tomorrow, and from here on out, no more chillin in the truck for me, unless I want to. I'll be joining him outside for the work day. Maybe I can catch one of those little idiot hairless guys doing pushups (skink? lizard? Gecko?). Or one of those GIANT RABBITS?! Or these huge black beetles. UGH I'm so excited. Screw Christmas, this is bigger.

Thanks cousin D. He also got me some bullshit dried beef twist thing that I think is for dogs... figured I'd like it anyway. But you helped buy my freedom and I'll be forever grateful 🙏❤️
